title: Dedicated capacity remediation scenarios, measurement windows, and contract text for throughput guarantees
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: produce canonical contract language and an operational playbook that define how Redwood measures and remedies shortfalls in committed dedicated throughput. This ticket scopes the measurable definitions, rolling windows, error-budget math, autoscaler interlock behavior, notification cadence, and suggested contractual clauses for remediation credits and operational obligations. We must balance observability precision, predictable customer economics, and on-call/operational safety. Output: 1) legal-ready contract snippets, 2) engineering SLO spec (measurement queries and dashboards), 3) Console notification templates and runbook steps.
acceptance_criteria: Quantitative SLO defined: metric name, collection window, aggregation function and target (e.g., 99th percentile tokens-per-minute delivered across committed fleet over 30-minute rolling windows)
Error budget computation documented: sliding-window math, weighting for short-lived spikes vs sustained degradation, and example credit calculations for monthly billing cycles
Autoscaler interlock behavior specified: thresholds that trigger temporary burst, cordon, and proportional throttling along with safe rollback behavior
Contract language drafted: plain-language clause for credits, notice windows, force-majeure carveouts, customer proactivity obligations, and dispute resolution path
Engineering artifacts: PromQL/SQL measurement queries, sample dashboard mockups, and a synthetic test harness for simulating degradation scenarios
Operational runbook: notification templates (email/console), escalation ladder, and automated remedial actions (failover to lower-fidelity model, prioritized request gating)
Legal and Sales sign-off obtained on proposed credit table and notice cadence
comments: 2026-02-12 - Kickoff: Alignment with Eng and Legal. Discussed trade-offs: short rolling windows give faster detection but increase noise. Agreed to pilot 30m rolling windows with quantile smoothing.

2026-02-18 - Engineering note (Diego): Prom approach recommended: derive per-customer committed_tokens_per_minute; compute delivered_tokens_per_minute as sum of successful generation tokens. Plan to emit 30s granularity metrics and roll up to 30m windows during query time.

2026-02-23 - Legal feedback (J. Patel): Prefer explicit remediation tiers rather than open-ended 'reasonable efforts'. Requested examples for credit computation and an initial cap (e.g., credits not to exceed 100% of monthly committed fees).

2026-03-01 - PM update: Drafted three remediation scenarios: (A) transient AZ blip <10m -> no credit but automated retry; (B) degraded throughput for 10-120m -> proportional credits based on deficit; (C) sustained multi-hour outage -> full remediation playbook incl. root-cause timeline and elevated credits. Need numeric thresholds for banding.

2026-03-05 - Engineering review: Concern about gaming the metric via client-side burst shaping. Proposed guardrail: baseline smoothing and a min-observed-traffic floor to avoid crediting low-util customers disproportionately.

2026-03-10 - UX/Console hooks: Recommend per-contract portal showing committed band, current burn-rate, projected exhaustion, and one-click request to open remediation claim. UX will consume same Prom endpoints as billing.

2026-03-14 - Draft contract excerpt shared with Sales: included definitions block (Committed Throughput; Delivered Throughput; Measurement Window; Error Budget), notification windows, credit table, and escalation anchors. Awaiting Sales review for customer-facing language adjustments.
proposed_contract_text: Definitions: 'Committed Throughput' means the tokens-per-minute capacity Redwood has reserved and agreed to deliver to Customer for the Service Period. 'Delivered Throughput' means the actual tokens-per-minute delivered by Redwood's fleet as measured by Redwood's telemetry in the Measurement Window.

Service Commitment: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Delivered Throughput that meets or exceeds 95% of Committed Throughput measured over rolling 30-minute windows for at least 99% of windows each monthly billing cycle.

Error Budget & Credits: If the Delivered Throughput falls below the Commitment, Customer will be eligible for a credit computed as (Committed - Delivered) / Committed * Billing Factor, where Billing Factor is defined in the contract tier table. Credits are capped at 100% of the monthly committed fee. Credits apply only after Customer provides written notice within 10 business days of the observed shortfall and after Customer has followed the remediation steps in the runbook.

Autoscaler Interlock & Remediation: Redwood may temporarily burst beyond contractual capacity to mitigate transient degradation. When sustained deficits occur (windows failing for >30 minutes), Redwood will: 1) trigger automated failover policies; 2) notify Customer via email and Console alert; 3) if not resolved within remediation SLAs, apply credits per the Error Budget formula.
engineering_notes: Metric design: emit per-customer committed_capacity and delivered_tokens with 30s resolution; aggregate at 30m sliding windows for SLO evaluation.
Smoothing: use weighted moving median to reduce credit churn from short tails. Expose both raw windows and smoothed series for audits.

Autoscaler behavior: define three modes - Normal, Burst-Protected, and Cordon. Burst-Protected allows short-duration extra allocation; Cordon restricts new session starts for non-critical routes while preserving existing sessions.
Test harness: create chaosmonkey scenarios that simulate AZ loss, degraded NVLink bandwidth, and kernel OOM to validate measurement and credit behavior.
risks_and_mitigations: Metric spoofing risk: mitigate by requiring a minimum observed baseline and cross-verifying request-level traces when credits are disputed.
Operational cost: unlimited credits could be abused; mitigation: caps, notice windows, and customer proactivity requirements (e.g., must enable specific telemetry).
Complexity to Sales: too many tiers / math confuses customers; mitigation: produce a simple one-page summary and an appendix with the full formula.
